brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A green tea from Jinggangshan in Jiangxi, grown around Shiji village, Huaguoshan, Tongmuling and Liping.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It was named one of Jiangxi's eight famous teas in 1982 and received a quality product award from the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Fishery in 1985. Little more is documented about its past.
processing: After brief spreading, the leaf passes through eight steps: fixing, first rolling, re-firing, second rolling, strand shaping, ball rubbing, raising the down and baking.
harvest_season: Mostly picked around Guyu, in late April.
appearance_dry: Fine, tight, hooked strands, emerald and downy.
appearance_wet: Whole, tender green and bright; in the cup the buds drift down and open like orchid flowers.
taste_profile: Fresh, tender aroma with a sweet, mellow taste.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
